nucleus.thesis: Door 3: Location is diagnostic, not determinative. Match work structure to team communication maturity, using remote as a forcing function that reveals whether async protocols can actually work.

claims.text: Intentional asynchronous design matters more than physical location. Remote makes this requirement visible; in-office teams can hide poor communication through synchronous proximity.
Tacit knowledge transfer happens via exposure to expertise, not location. Both pair programming and async code review with detailed commentary enable osmosis when deliberately designed.
Remote work exposes organizational dysfunction that offices mask. For healthy teams, this exposure becomes a diagnostic advantage; for dysfunctional teams, it becomes a liability.
Hybrid output-based teams with 2–3 daily core hours for high-bandwidth moments capture both osmosis and deep focus, making location optional based on actual communication maturity.
The burden of proof flips: not 'can remote work with extraordinary maturity?' but 'which structure forces teams to build real collaboration skills?' Remote is the faster diagnostic.

shell.topic: Is remote work better than in-office for software teams?

adjacency.target: work design from location-first to maturity-first
